required_tuples.rationale: The entry document contains id="__nuxt" and names a real /_nuxt/<hash>.js that is served as JavaScript without authentication, a known client route returns the identical entry bytes, all at the configured base path.
A missing /_nuxt asset and the /_nuxt/ directory answer 404, and neither the entry document nor a directory listing (0180c66.js exists in client/dist/_nuxt) is returned.

With ROUTER_BASE_PATH=/client-prefix the entry document (id="__nuxt", naming a /_nuxt/<hash>.js) and that script, served as JavaScript, are both fetched successfully under the prefix without authentication.
A fresh install answers /ping and /status with isInit false and the exact ConfigPath/MetadataPath the process was started with.
On the initialized fixture install two /status reads are byte-identical with isInit true/app/version, /ping answers twice and two device logins both return an access token.
POST /init on a fresh install returns 200, flips /status from isInit false with paths to isInit true without paths, and the new root credentials return a token that /api/me resolves to that username.
GET /status stays 200 with an identical body for an unauthenticated and a stale-bearer request, and the public GET route also answers HEAD /ping with 200 and an empty body.
A fixture user's login with a wrong password is 401 and the users and sessions row counts are unchanged.
The process is launched with only PORT in the environment (the harness never passes --port), the selected port is not 3333, and /ping answers on it.
With PORT naming one port and --port another, /ping answers on the flag-selected port and (when the ports differ) the environment-selected port refuses connections.
With CONFIG_PATH/METADATA_PATH in the environment and --config/--metadata flags pointing elsewhere, a fresh /status reports exactly the flag directories and not the environment CONFIG_PATH.
HOST=999.999.999.999 alone exits non-zero and answers no HTTP, while the same environment with --host 127.0.0.1 serves /ping on loopback.
ROUTER_BASE_PATH=/launch-prefix makes /launch-prefix/ping and /launch-prefix/status serve the boot contract while the default /audiobookshelf/ping no longer answers.
PORT=99999 exits non-zero without answering /ping, and a later normal boot of the same fresh install serves /ping.
PORT set to a filesystem path never serves the TCP /ping liveness answer on the harness port within the readiness window (upstream binds a named socket instead).
A restart on the same install and options answers /status with an identical body and /ping 200, before and after.
One fresh boot serves /ping {success:true}, /status isInit false with app audiobookshelf and serverVersion 2.37.2, an HTML entry document at / and 401 from the auth-gated /api/libraries.
A second process on the same fixture tree serves /ping, isInit true, the identical sorted library ids and user count, and the stored root user can still log in.
A garbage absdatabase.sqlite makes the boot exit non-zero without answering /ping, the supplied database bytes are unchanged, and no -journal/-wal/-shm sidecar appears beside it.
A CONFIG_PATH that is a regular file makes the boot exit non-zero without answering /ping, the supplied file's bytes are unchanged and its containing directory still lists exactly [config].
A 0500 METADATA_PATH never answers /ping within the readiness window and the directory stays empty.
